correctness.rationale: For each 1<=k<p^a the exact Lucas-theorem valuation of C(p^a,k) is a-v_p(k); only k=j p^(a-1) survive after cubing modulo p^4, and their units yield S_p=Σ(-1)^(j-1)/j^3. For p>=5, the full reciprocal-cube sum vanishes and Bernoulli-polynomial evaluation of the half-sum yields S_p=B_(p-3)/2 mod p. For p=2 or 3 the coefficient is nonzero, giving exact valuation 3. Glaisher gives the independent central-binomial equivalence. The verifier reconstructed direct modular values, Bernoulli numbers and critical units; no finite extrapolation is used.

The published statement has no explicit initial coefficient B_(p-3)/2 and no Wolstenholme exception criterion.

Direct finite-index binomial reduction was proved separately.

originality.rationale: The new part of this theorem is the explicit Bernoulli coefficient and equivalence of p^4 Franel divisibility with Wolstenholme primes. Straub (arXiv:1401.0854, Example 3.6) already proves much stronger height-stability congruences for the same Franel numbers and is explicitly acknowledged; no novelty is claimed for height stability alone. Read relevant primary sources and compared exact implications as well as published mathematical-result records and accessible historical claims; later equivalent formulations remain a residual risk.

value.rationale: The specific new datum is the initial p^4 Franel residue B_(p-3)/2, whose vanishing gives a natural Franel-theoretic characterization of Wolstenholme primes and excludes nonexceptional proper prime powers in a recorded prime-detection conjecture. Strong prime-power height stability is already proved by Straub and is not valued as an original contribution. The Bernoulli identification is a complete, arithmetic, motivated local invariant; valuations above p^4 at Wolstenholme primes are not resolved.
